scenes.title: Choose what to learn
scenes.visual: Founder reviews anonymous snapshot, journey and landscape maps.
scenes.narration: Your earlier work has surfaced assumptions and unknowns. A discovery research plan turns them into practical learning steps. Choose one or two uncertainties that could change your focus. Planning research is not collecting evidence, and completion does not validate a business.

scenes.title: Reach relevant people ethically
scenes.visual: Adult participant can accept or decline a conversation.
scenes.narration: Describe the relevant group and context, how you can reach them, and who may be missing. Start with a small feasible learning round, not a claim of a representative sample. Ask permission, make participation voluntary, and avoid people over whom you hold authority when it could create pressure.

scenes.title: Match methods to questions
scenes.visual: Editable observe, ask and read cards.
scenes.narration: Choose a method for each uncertainty. Observe permitted actions, ask about a recent experience, or inspect a relevant document. Record what each method can and cannot tell you. Do not pitch a solution and treat polite approval as evidence of demand.

scenes.title: Prepare neutral prompts
scenes.narration: Ask what happened the last time, what the person tried, and what mattered. Avoid leading questions such as wouldn’t our app make this easier. Plan a permitted observation checklist without guessing emotions. Use anonymous source codes and collect only information needed for the question.

scenes.title: Plan timing and review
scenes.visual: Editable owner, permission, time and review cards.
scenes.narration: Set the owner, timing, effort limit, permission needed and fallback if access fails. Decide how to record evidence, interpretations and unknowns separately. Name a review date and signals that could support, weaken or change your focus. Do not promise that a fixed number of conversations proves demand.

scenes.title: Close the learning module
scenes.visual: Actual approved Lesson 15 worksheet recording and five-deliverable list.
scenes.narration: Create your Discovery Research Plan and review your customer snapshot, journey map, source log and market landscape. These five deliverables close Module 1.3 when each lesson is locally complete. Research execution remains a next action. The next module turns your provisional problem into an opportunity hypothesis.

children: A
research plan

connects a question to a method, relevant people or sources, practical access and a review decision. It is a plan, not findings. Start with one or two uncertainties from Lessons 11–14 that could change your focus.
Match the method to the question
Observe
Record permitted actions and context. Do not infer feelings from appearance or disrupt the experience.
Ask
Ask adults about recent experiences; preserve their account as reported information. Avoid pitching or pressuring agreement.
Read
Inspect relevant sources with date, scope and limits. Provider claims do not establish customer outcomes.
Review
Separate evidence, interpretation and unknowns. Look for conflicting information and choose the next check.
Neutral prompts
“Tell me about the last time you tried to find registration.” “What did you try?” “What happened next?” “What mattered most?” These are more useful than “Wouldn’t our app solve this?”
Permission and practical limits

Define voluntary participation, permission for the setting and a simple way to decline or stop. Use anonymous roles/source codes; avoid private contact details and sensitive information. Do not record audio, images or video without appropriate permission. This prototype does not contact or recruit anyone.

Set a feasible learning round, owner, time limit, fallback and review date. A few conversations may reveal clues but do not establish representativeness or demand. Record who your access plan may exclude.

Simulated Coach · no AI connection
Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: Connect priority unknowns to methods, ethical access and a review decision. A plan is not collected evidence.
replies.guide: Set relevant people/sources, neutral prompts, pending permissions, owner/timing, anonymous notes and a fallback. Define what would change your focus.
replies.review: Research Plan check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify permission, recruit participants, execute research or establish demand.
replies.challenge: Are prompts leading? Can people decline? Who is excluded? What contradicts your focus? Is there a realistic fallback if access fails?

More questions to discuss

Can people freely decline? Are you relying only on friends or convenient contacts? Are methods suitable for the question? Are you collecting unnecessary private data? Have you confused planning with completed research?
Answer all three. You can retry; all three correct are required for local completion.
